title: Same contacts, different order
hook: Four contacts join A to E. Does the order they happen in change who can catch it?

knows: a "who is connected to whom" diagram
doesNotKnow: that infection can only move forward in time, so the same contacts in another order reach different people

misconception: If you can trace a chain of contacts from the first case to someone, that person is at risk. (A contact diagram ignores when each contact happened.)
objective: The learner can explain that infection only crosses a contact that happens after the carrier was infected, so the same contacts in a different order reach different people (reversed, only B; forward, all four), and that overlapping contacts open paths in both directions.

claims.text: The lesson's rule: the first case is infected on day 0; infection crosses a contact on its day only if one side was infected on an earlier day, and every such contact passes it on. So infection only moves forward in time.
claims.source: The lesson's toy rule (brief claim 1; spec company/design/specs/contact-order-matters.md 'The rule'). Stage rule line: 'Infection crosses a contact whenever one side was infected on an earlier day.' Implemented as spread() in Demo.tsx. Deliberately certain; see c7.

claims.text: With A as the first case, in the order E→A (D-E day 1, C-D day 2, B-C day 3, A-B day 4) only B is reached, on day 4; A met B only after the other contacts were over. In the order A→E (A-B day 1, B-C day 2, C-D day 3, D-E day 4) all four are reached, one per day.
claims.source: Node re-run 2026-10-14 by the builder with spread() copied from Demo.tsx: E→A from A reached by day 0..4 = 0,0,0,0,1 (B@4); A→E from A = 0,1,2,3,4 (B@1 C@2 D@3 E@4). Deterministic, no seed. Answers the prediction (D-E, C-D, B-C, A-B gives 1).

claims.text: Overlap: every pair meets on each of days 1 to 4, with no relay on the same day. Infection then reaches all four people from either end, one person per day.
claims.source: Rule from brief claim 3 and the spec (accepted as a drawing in company/design/reviews/2026-10-14-design-review-ncm-specs.md §5). Node re-run 2026-10-14 with spread() from Demo.tsx: from A, B@1 C@2 D@3 E@4; from E, D@1 C@2 B@3 A@4.

claims.text: With E as the first case, the order A→E reaches only D (on day 4). Shown in the reveal only if the learner reached that state.
claims.source: Node re-run 2026-10-14 with spread() from Demo.tsx: A→E from E reached by day 0..4 = 0,0,0,0,1 (D@4). (Also checked, not quoted: E→A from E reaches all four.)

claims.text: The same contacts can expose or protect someone depending on their order, so a diagram of who met whom overstates who can be reached.
claims.source: From c1: a person is reached only along a chain of contacts with increasing days, which is a subset of the chains in the undated diagram; c2 shows the subset can be strictly smaller (1 of 4 vs 4 of 4) for the same contacts.

claims.text: Overlapping (concurrent) partnerships can spread infection further than the same partnerships in sequence (Morris and Kretzschmar, 1997).
claims.source: Morris M, Kretzschmar M (1997), 'Concurrent partnerships and the spread of HIV', AIDS 11(5). NEEDS A HUMAN SOURCE CHECK by the fact-checker, including the citation details (cited from the brief; the builder had no access to the paper). The disease is deliberately not named to learners.

claims.text: Real contacts are not certain to pass an infection on (the lesson's every-contact-transmits rule is a deliberate simplification), and real contacts are not known in advance.
claims.source: Brief claim 5: disclosure that the stage is a toy model. The reveal shows only the first half ('Real contacts are not certain to pass it on').

recall.question: Two contacts: X met Y on Tuesday, and Y met Z on Monday. X was infected the week before. Under the rule that infection only crosses a contact after the carrier was infected, can X's infection reach Z through Y?
options: Yes: there is a chain X to Y to Z
No: Y met Z before Y was infected
Only if X and Z also meet
recall.why: Infection only moves forward in time. Y caught it on Tuesday, after the contact with Z was already over.

references.note: contact timing and concurrency; section unconfirmed (brief: § unconfirmed)
